area: endings: ending presentation (six endings: transition, identity, summary, verdict, distinctions, replay)
summary: All six endings open cleanly from play (no blank frame, no second dialog, no moving scene), carry the copydeck's verdict and section-11 copy word for word, earn their distinctions correctly, and keep New run and Replay on screen and keyboard-reachable at 1366x768 and on a phone. Eight things are worth a look: two wrong numbers (the Barely missed scene rounds the share of quota up, as far as "QUOTA 100%", while the card floors it; the Ascension card leaves out the quad shot that ended the run) and six presentation edges (the card overflowing a 768px-tall window, a 0.1 s flash of the dashboard after the quad-shot confirmation, two reduced-motion slips, truncated tiles on a small phone held sideways, a leftover caption).
verified_ok: Transitions, test build, crafted v2.1 runs one move from the end, 19 pictures each (every ~200 ms for 3 s, then every 2 s, then the card), 15 runs at 1366x768 and 8 at 390x844 touch: club, missed, fired (review, org, QBR under 70%, politics at 100%), repo (rent, a conference at -$700, a clAInk Friday invoice, a clAInk strike-3 true-up), meltdown (an action at 99 stress, the weekend roll), ascension (certain shot with its confirmation, heart roll on shot 3). In every one the ending dialog is up 0.09-0.17 s after the press with its title and company line in the first frame, the CRT switches on and plays, exactly one dialog is open throughout (a Friday event scripted into the same week as a firing does not stack a choice on it), the dialog's size and place do not change until the card, and there were 0 page or console errors. Scripts and pictures: test-results/audit/endings/ (transitions.cjs, trans-*.png, trans-*.json).

The announcer's line arriving mid-scene does not move the scene: header 64px before and after on desktop, 109px on phones; the longest line (HR's 'We've reviewed the situation and are ending your employment.') takes 2 lines in the reserved space at 320x568, 375x667 and 390x844 (capjump.cjs). Nothing from the final move is voiced as a play caption (src/engine/audio/director.js:11) and the ending's header never showed a line from play.

The paperwork unfolding on desktop is a 0.5 s eased slide, not a jump: at 1440x900 the scene moves 297 -> 142 px with at most 21 px between two animation frames; at 1366x768 at most 31 px (unfold.cjs). On phones the dialog is top-anchored and the scene's top stays put (184 px before and after the card).

Identity, release build, finished v2.1 runs: six different titles, company lines, scenes, caption bands and verdicts (sheet-id-1440.png, sheet-id-phone.png). At 1440x900 all six finished cards are whole with nothing scrolled (the tallest, Ascension with two notes and a distinction, is 828 of 876 px). At 390x844 five of six are whole. With reduced motion at 1440x900 each shows the scene's last frame, its one-sentence description and the card at once (sheet-id-reduced-1440.png). Club reads triumphant and faintly ridiculous (gold jacket, dollar fireworks, 'Next quarter: Higher quota.'); Terminated reads cold (badge reader, HR's line, 'Reason on file: ...').

Summary arithmetic against the run the page saved, 37 cards (transitions and cards.cjs): Closed equals closedWon; percent is floored (159,999 -> 99%, 160,000 -> 100%, 111,999 -> 69%, 9,000 -> 5%); cash after the last move (6,240 + 1,000 salary = 7,240; -950 + 1,000 - 1,600 rent = -1,550; -700 - 800 = -1,500; 3,000 + 12% of 70,000 + 1,000 = 12,400); negative cash in red with a true minus sign; Deals signed and '2 lost' equal the story's counts, a deal signed by play raised 9 to 10 and replaced the largest deal with 'Feral Unicorn $70,000'; 'Deals signed (incl. reversed)' when revenue was clawed back; a save with no story shows only Closed, Cash and what else it can vouch for (Discounts given, Left in pipeline).

Verdict and copy: 58 strings of copydeck section 11 compared by script with src/copy/endings.js and scenes.js (six verdicts, seven dialog bodies, the caption sets a and b, 23 story cards, seven distinction subtitles, 'For the record'): all equal (copydeck.mjs). The verdict rendered on each card is that ending's; the four 'Reason on file' lines match their causes; a politics firing at 100% shows Terminated, a repossession at 103% shows Jacket repo'd, never Club.

Distinctions, each earned and each withheld (cards.cjs, 22 runs, all as expected): The American Dream on a repo at 103% and not at 99%; The Right Stuff on every Ascension; Whale hunter after a real $70,000 close push; Digital Transformation when billed 1,400 > earned 900, not at 900 = 900, hidden when the commission is unknown; A Natural Leader after a rebalance took the largest deal (by play) and from a recorded take; Vice President of Optics at manager exactly 100 under quota, not at 99.15, not over quota; Expense Account Patriot on the third conference (by play), hidden for a pre-2.1 story; at most three, in the copydeck's order (americanDream, whale, digital, when five apply); no Distinctions block when none apply.

Replay and New run (replay.cjs, played to Club by keyboard at 1366x768, 390x844 touch and 667x375 touch): both buttons inside the window and on top while the scene plays and after the card (1366x768: Replay at y 703-739, New run at 703-739 of 768); focus opens on 'Skip to the end'; Escape three times changes nothing; Enter skips, the card comes in and focus moves to New run; Shift+Tab reaches Replay; Enter replays the scene (caption retyped from '> PRES', plays to its last frame, card stays, focus stays); Tab reaches New run; Enter starts week 1 with focus on End week. Auto-repeat of a held Enter or Space is swallowed (src/shell/shell.js:24-28).

The ten finished runs saved by an older version (test/saves/fixtures/generated/end-*.json) open on the release build with the right ending, cause line and verdict and no errors (fixtures.cjs). For a screen reader the dialog is named 'Week 9 of 13 Terminated', the scene is an image labelled with its one-sentence description, and the card is hidden until it arrives (a11y.cjs).

No number or name on the card is cut at 1440x900, 1366x768, 1024x768, 768x1024, 390x844, 375x667, 320x568, 844x390, 932x430 or 1024x500 (trunc.cjs). No tracked file was changed (git status is clean); everything written is under test-results/audit/endings/.

findings.title: Barely missed: the cutscene rounds the share of quota up (it can say QUOTA 100%), the card floors it
findings.where: src/ui/Game.jsx:199 (hands the scene the exact fraction as meta.pct) -> src/engine/scenes/defs/missed.js:40 and :50 (Math.round); the card floors at src/game/selectors.js:80
findings.evidence: Release build, a finished run that closed $159,600 (99.75%): during the scene the bar reads 'QUOTA 100%' with STALLED under it, next to the '100%' marker (test-results/audit/endings/missed100-bar.png); on the finished card the shop sign reads '100% OFF' directly above the tile '99% of quota' (missed100-card.png). A run at $151,200 (94.5%): sign '95% OFF', tile '94% of quota' (id-1440x900-missed.png). The engine's own text render gives 'QUOTA 100%' and '100% OFF' for $159,200 to $159,999, 95 against 94 at $151,200, 71 against 70 at $112,800 (missedpct.cjs). Over every dollar amount from $112,000 to $159,999 the scene and the card disagree for exactly half (24,000 of 48,000). CHANGELOG.md:15 (2.1) says 'Percentages are floored', and the log line floors too ('Q1 final: 99% of quota').
findings.proposal: Hand the scene the floored share, in the interface only: src/ui/Game.jsx:199, pct: s.quota>0 ? Math.floor(100*s.closedWon/s.quota)/100 : 0. Checked for every dollar from $112,000 to $159,999: the scene's Math.round then prints the card's number with 0 mismatches. The engine and its pictures are untouched (only missed.js reads meta.pct; the bar's fill stays 39 of 40 cells at 99%).
findings.risk: The number in the Barely missed scene drops by one for runs whose share has a fraction of .5 or more. The scene parity test is unaffected: it feeds meta straight to the engine (test/parity/scenes.cjs:54-56).

findings.title: Ascension: the card's quad-shot count leaves out the shot that ended the run
findings.where: src/game/story.js:8 (only the log tag coffee.shot is counted; the fatal shot is logged as end.ascension instead, src/game/actions.js:167-171) -> src/game/selectors.js:84 -> src/ui/Ending.jsx:24 (the 'Quad shots' tile) and :40 (the 'N quad shots. Facilities unplugged the machine.' note, from 5)
findings.evidence: Test build, Quad shot pressed three times in week 4 with the third shot's heart roll scripted to fail: the cutscene's caption says 'Shot #3.', the log says 'Quad shot #3. Your departure velocity exceeded expectations.', the dashboard chip behind the dialog says '3 quad shots', and the card's tile says 'Quad shots 2' (test-results/audit/endings/card-shots-off-by-one.png; the saved run has coffeesThisWeek 3 and story.n.shots 2). A run with four earlier shots that drinks two more, the second fatal, gets the note '5 quad shots. Facilities unplugged the machine.' after six (cards.json, shots-note-off-by-one). It happens on every Ascension, because the fatal shot never writes coffee.shot.
findings.proposal: Count the fatal shot where the card reads the number: src/game/selectors.js:84, shots: st ? (st.n.shots || 0) + (s.endCause === "caffeine" ? 1 : 0) : null (endCause is 'caffeine' only when a quad shot ended the run). Display only: the story, the save and the rules stay as they are, and Ascensions saved earlier are corrected as well.
findings.risk: On an Ascension the note 'N quad shots...' appears one shot sooner (its threshold is 5), and a first-shot Ascension with nothing signed gains a 'Quad shots 1' tile. No test reads runFacts().shots (grep of test/). The other fix, adding "end.ascension" to COUNTS in story.js, changes saved state and would show in the frozen-engine equivalence check.

findings.title: 1366x768: the finished card is taller than the window, so the scroll to the paperwork slices the first line or takes the title off screen
findings.where: src/ui/Ending.jsx:63 (the scene gets 16px type from 760px of window height) and :94-104 (whatever scrolls is taken to its end); src/styles/dialogs.css:2 (max-height 100dvh - 24px)
findings.evidence: Release build, finished cards at 1366x768 (identity.json): the dialog can show 742px. Club and meltdown with two notes need 766 and are scrolled 24px: 'Week 13 of 13' and the announcer's line are cut through the middle (test-results/audit/endings/trans-1366x768-club-19-card.png). Fired needs 762 (20px). Ascension, which always carries The Right Stuff, needs 801 to 826 and is scrolled 59 to 84px: the overline and the title 'Ascension' are gone, and with two notes the company's line is sliced (trans-1366x768-ascension-19-card.png, trans-1366x768-ascension-roll-19-card.png); a repossession with a distinction likewise (826). Missed and repo with one note fit (741). Parts: header 64, line 33, scene 332, verdict 67, tiles 104, notes 86, distinctions 61, footer 64; without 2.1's verdict and distinctions the same card is 698 and fitted. On 390x844 only Ascension overflows (866 to 891 of 818: title cut, trans-phone-ascension-19-card.png). The QA matrix did not meet this because it opens the old end-*.json fixtures, whose cards have no notes (test/e2e/matrix.cjs:59-64).
findings.proposal: Let the scene take its smaller step until the whole card fits: src/ui/Ending.jsx:63, h>=760 ? 16 : 14 becomes h>=860 ? 16 : 14. Measured with 14px type (1366x759): club 727, missed 702, fired 723, repo 702, meltdown 727, all inside the 742px a 768px window gives, so five of the six finished cards show whole with nothing scrolled. Ascension needs 787 and still scrolls 45px (overline gone, title at the edge).
findings.risk: Windows 760 to 859px tall (1366x768, 1024x768, 1280x800) get the scene at 14px type, 538px wide instead of 614px, for the whole ending and not only the card. Upright phones and tablets are limited by width and do not change. Ascension's title is still not fully on screen at 768.

findings.title: Quad-shot confirmation to Ascension: the dashboard flashes at full brightness between the two dialogs
findings.where: src/ui/Game.jsx:318 (the confirmation closes and the move runs; the ending opens a commit later, :184-204) and src/styles/dialogs.css:7 (every dialog's backdrop fades in from 0 over .16s)
findings.evidence: Sampled every animation frame after pressing 'Drink it anyway' (handover.cjs): the confirmation with its full backdrop at 14 ms; no dialog open at 36 ms; the ending open at opacity 0 with backdrop 0 from 55 to 82 ms; backdrop 0.10 at 103 ms, 0.54 at 148 ms, 1.0 at 234 ms. A second run: less than half dimmed for 106 ms (7 frames). Screencast frames at 41 and 87 ms show the whole desk bright with no dialog, between a dimmed frame before and a dimmed frame after (test-results/audit/endings/sheet-handover-coffee.png, trans-1366x768-ascension-01-f0.png). The first Hail Mary's confirmation does the same when the throw ends the run at 100 stress (no dialog at 62 ms, backdrop 0 until 103 ms). A plain End week into an ending only dims; there is nothing to flash.
findings.proposal: One rule in src/styles/dialogs.css: dialog.ending::backdrop{animation:none}. Tried by injecting that rule into the frozen build at run time (handover-fix.cjs): the undimmed gap falls from 106 ms (7 frames) to 18 ms (1 frame).
findings.risk: On every ending the dim behind the dialog arrives at once instead of fading in over 0.16 s; the dialog itself still fades in. One undimmed frame remains, because the ending opens one commit after the confirmation closes.

findings.title: Reduced motion: the ending opens already scrolled to its end, so on a phone or a 768px window the title and the company's line are never shown
findings.where: src/ui/Ending.jsx:94-104 (the scroll meant to follow the paperwork; with reduced motion the card is in at 0 ms and so is the scroll)
findings.evidence: Release build with prefers-reduced-motion. 390x844 touch: club and meltdown open scrolled 39px (overline gone, title at the very edge), fired 35, Ascension 140: the dialog opens on '...building's jurisdiction.' with no overline, no title and half of its first sentence (test-results/audit/endings/id-390x844t-reduced-ascension.png). 1366x768: club 51, fired 47, Ascension 131, with the title, the line and the top of the still off screen (id-1366x768-reduced-ascension.png). Reached by play as well: 350 ms after End week the dialog is at scrollTop 39 of 39 (reducedplay-390x844t.png). With motion the same scroll comes only after the 7 to 9 s scene, during which the title is on screen. At 1440x900 nothing scrolls.
findings.proposal: Do not run that scroll when there was no scene to watch first: at the top of the effect at src/ui/Ending.jsx:94, return when REDUCED_MOTION is set or there is no scene engine. The dialog then opens at its first line like every other dialog (the Modal already sets scrollTop to 0 when it opens).
findings.risk: With reduced motion on a small screen the lower part of the paperwork starts under the pinned buttons and has to be scrolled to, as in the handbook; on phones the footer already has an edge that says so (src/styles/dialogs.css:35).

findings.title: Reduced motion: the announcer's ending line is captioned behind the dialog on a desktop and not at all on a phone
findings.where: src/engine/scenes/player.js:375 (under reduced motion the scene's key cues, the announcer's line among them, fire inside play(), before the dialog is open) -> src/ui/captions.js:11 (modal is false, so the line goes to the top bar) -> src/styles/app.css:252 (hidden under a dialog on phones)
findings.evidence: Release build, reduced motion (reducedcap.cjs): at 1440x900 the ending's header never shows a caption for club or fired, while the top bar behind the backdrop shows 'PA President's Club. Please retain your boarding pass.' and 'HR As of today, your position with Shitcorp has ended.' for 4 s (test-results/audit/endings/sheet-id-reduced-1440.png). At 390x844 the same line sits in the bottom notice with visibility:hidden for its whole 4 s, so it is never seen, and the header keeps the two empty lines it reserves for it (reducedplay-390x844t.png). With motion the line appears in the header 5 to 7 s in.
findings.proposal: Let the reduced-motion cues fire one tick after play() returns: src/engine/scenes/player.js:375, wrap that line in the player's own later(function(){ ... },0). The mechanism was checked on the frozen build by asking the page's audio engine for the line once the dialog was open: it is captioned in the header at 390x844 and at 1440x900, with the header height and the scene's position unchanged (reducedcap-fix.cjs).
findings.risk: It touches the scene player (the timing of sound cues only, no picture). The boot screen under reduced motion shares the path, and an audio test that expects those cues synchronously would need the tick. stop() already clears the timer.

findings.title: A small phone on its side (667x375): the card's numbers are cut with an ellipsis ('$171,3...')
findings.where: src/styles/dialogs.css:65-67 (four tiles across, nowrap with ellipsis) inside the landscape layout at :96-106; the two-by-two rule at :89-90 applies only up to 640px of width
findings.evidence: Release build, 667x375 touch: the tiles are 102px wide; 'Closed $171,300' needs 77px and has 70, shown as '$171,3...'; '107% of quota' needs 88, shown as '107% of ...'; 'Quasar Laundry' needs 98, shown as 'Quasar L...' (test-results/audit/endings/replay-667x375-card.png; trunc.cjs). At 740x360 only the account name is cut (needs 98, has 88). Nothing is cut at 844x390, 932x430 or any upright or desktop size tried.
findings.proposal: Give a narrow landscape window the phone's two-by-two tiles: add to src/styles/dialogs.css @media (max-height:600px) and (orientation:landscape) and (max-width:800px){ .end-fact{flex:1 1 50%} .end-fact dd.end-sub{white-space:normal} } (the same two declarations as lines 89-90).
findings.risk: The card is one row of tiles taller on those phones; it already scrolls beside the scene there. This rule was not tried in a build.

findings.title: Desktop: the announcer's caption from the move before the fatal one stays in the top bar behind the ending
findings.where: src/ui/app/TopBar.jsx:12-17 (a caption keeps its 4 to 9 s); src/styles/app.css:252 hides it under a dialog only inside the phone block
findings.evidence: Test build, 1366x768: a CRM cleanup (announcer: 'Pipeline hygiene is everyone's responsibility.'), then a conference that takes cash to -$1,500. Half a second into 'Jacket repo'd' the top bar, dimmed behind the backdrop, still reads 'PA Pipeline hygiene is everyone's responsibility.' (test-results/audit/endings/leftover-1366x768.png); it has gone by the time the scene's own line arrives (5.7 s). At 390x844 it is hidden. It is never inside the ending's dialog.
findings.proposal: Move the rule at src/styles/app.css:252 (html:has(dialog[open]) .pa-cap{visibility:hidden}) out of the max-width:640px block so it holds at every width.
findings.risk: A caption that is on screen when any dialog opens (the handbook, a Friday choice) is hidden on a desktop too, and shows again if its time is not up when the dialog closes.

not_checked: Sound: the stingers, the announcer's voice and the heartbeat were not heard (headless Chromium); only the captions' words, place and timing were checked.
Other browsers: only Chromium exists here. The dashboard flash, the card's grid-rows unfold and the scroll may behave differently in Firefox and Safari.

Real devices: phones and the landscape phone are Chromium's touch emulation; a real 1366x768 laptop has less height than its screen (at a 1366x657 viewport every finished card is scrolled 70 to 156px and loses its title), which I measured but did not picture card by card.
A whole quarter played from week 1: every ending was reached from a crafted run one to three presses from the end with scripted dice, not from thirteen weeks of play.

The proposed changes themselves: nothing was built. Two were tried by injection on the frozen build (the backdrop rule; a line spoken after the dialog is open), one by arithmetic (the floored share); the scene-type threshold was inferred from a 1366x759 window; the shot count, the reduced-motion scroll guard and the landscape tile rule were not run.
The project's own suites (npm scripts, scripts/verify.mjs) were not run, as instructed, so I cannot say which existing assertions the proposals would touch beyond what a grep of test/ shows.
The scenes' pictures against 2.0.1 frame by frame (the QA's 1,718-frame comparison) were not repeated; I only looked at them.
Endings at 200% zoom, at 768x1024 and at 320x568 were not pictured card by card (only the truncation check and the caption check ran there).

Under reduced motion the ending opens with the focus on New run (there is no scene button to hold it), so a second separate press of Enter after End week would start a new run; I saw the focus but did not test the double press.
